Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Portal and ad lead capture with instant response and qualification

Enquiries from property portals, Meta and Google lead forms, the website and missed-call numbers reach one CRM queue within seconds, are deduplicated and answered with approved project content, then qualified and assigned to an executive with response-time alerts.

Residential developers · Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Portal and ad leads arrive at all hours into separate dashboards and inboxes. The same buyer enquires on several portals, nobody owns the first call, and slow follow-up wastes media spend. Generic chatbots, meanwhile, risk quoting the wrong price or promising a possession date.

Trigger

A lead arrives through a portal push or pull integration (99acres, MagicBricks or Housing.com, for example), a Meta or Google lead form, the website, a missed-call number or a QR code on a hoarding.

How it runs

  • Normalize the phone number and project, match the lead against CRM records by phone, email and portal lead ID, and merge duplicates while keeping every source for attribution.
  • Read the consent captured by the source form: opted-in leads get an approved WhatsApp template with the brochure, RERA registration number and next steps; others get a call from the assigned executive, who offers the opt-in.
  • Collect configuration, budget band, preferred location, purchase timeline, home-loan need and resident or NRI status through a short WhatsApp Flow or the executive's call script.
  • Answer questions on amenities, location, carpet area and price range only from the approved project knowledge base, citing the entry used; offers, discounts and possession dates are handed to the executive.
  • Score the lead against rules the sales head sets, assign it by project, language or round robin, and alert the sales manager when no meaningful contact happens within the agreed window.
  • Report response time, qualification and cost per qualified lead by source, campaign and portal package every week.

Human checkpoint

The assigned executive owns every qualified conversation and makes the first call where there is no WhatsApp opt-in. Prices come only from the approved price sheet; offers, discounts, payment-plan changes and possession dates go to the executive or sales manager. Marketing and legal approve all templates.

Data & consent

Unconverted leads are deleted or anonymized after the retention period the client sets. Model calls run under terms that exclude training on the data.

What we deliver

  • Approved WhatsApp templates and qualification Flow

  • Assignment rules and response-time alerts

How we measure it

  • Speed to first contact by source
  • Leads contacted within the agreed window
  • Qualified lead share
  • Duplicate lead rate
  • Cost per qualified lead

Discover and enquireStandard4–6 weeks

Channel partner client registration with duplicate and conflict checks

Partners register clients through a simple portal or WhatsApp form before a visit. Each registration is checked against existing leads and other partners, timestamped, confirmed with a validity period and linked to the visit, so attribution rests on evidence rather than memory.

Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

When two partners claim the same buyer, or a buyer who enquired directly arrives with a broker, the decision depends on screenshots and phone calls. Disputes sour partner relationships, delay brokerage and make partners reluctant to bring their best clients to the developer.

Trigger

An empanelled partner submits a client registration for a project through the partner portal or a WhatsApp Flow, or arrives at the sales gallery with a client who is not yet registered.

How it runs

  • Confirm the partner is empanelled for the project and that the RERA agent registration number on file is present and valid, and pause new registrations from partners whose registration has lapsed.
  • Normalize the client's phone and name, and record the partner's confirmation that the client agreed to share their details with the developer.
  • Check the client against direct leads, other partners' registrations and past bookings within the validity window set in the developer's written partner policy.
  • Confirm a clean registration to the partner with a reference number and expiry date; send possible duplicates to the partner manager with a timeline of every touch, without revealing other parties' details.
  • At the gallery, a QR check-in links the visit to the registration and alerts the partner; registrations near expiry prompt the partner to book a visit or renew under the policy.
  • Log every decision with its evidence for the brokerage stage and for monthly partner reviews.

Human checkpoint

The channel partner manager decides every flagged duplicate or conflict under the written partner policy, and the sales head hears appeals. The automation never rejects a disputed claim on its own, and partners see only their own registrations.

Discover and enquireStandard4–6 weeks

RFQ and BOQ intake with extraction, vendor quotes and bid tracking

Tender and RFQ emails become entries in a bid register. AI extracts BOQ line items from spreadsheets and PDFs into a structured sheet mapped to your rate library and flags missing specifications, and the team tracks quotes, clarifications and deadlines until the estimator signs off.

Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Estimators spend days retyping BOQs from PDFs and spreadsheets, vendor quotes come back late or not at all, and pre-bid and clarification deadlines are tracked in personal inboxes. Good tenders are missed and rushed bids carry pricing errors.

Trigger

An RFQ, tender notice or addendum arrives in the bids mailbox or is downloaded from a client or government e-procurement portal, with drawings, specifications and a BOQ.

How it runs

  • Create a bid record with client, scope, pre-bid and submission dates, earnest money and document list, and post a summary to the bid channel for a go or no-go decision.
  • Extract BOQ items, units and quantities from spreadsheets or PDFs into a structured sheet, keeping the original item numbers and page references.
  • Suggest matching codes from the contractor's rate library, and flag items with no match, unclear specifications or unusual quantities for the estimator.
  • Send quote requests for unmatched materials and subcontract packages to approved vendors, and chase replies before the internal cut-off.
  • Track pre-bid queries, client clarifications and addenda against the affected BOQ items, and remind owners of every deadline.
  • Record submission, opening results, published competitor rates and the win or loss reason for use in future bids.

Human checkpoint

The chief estimator reviews every extracted line against the source document and approves every rate; extraction stays a draft until checked. A director approves the go or no-go decision, the margin and the final submission.

Visit and evaluateStandard3–4 weeks

Site visit booking, reminders, check-in and post-visit follow-up

Qualified buyers book a site visit on WhatsApp against sales gallery capacity, receive reminders with the location pin, check in by QR code on arrival and get a feedback request afterwards, while the executive's notes become a confirmed CRM summary and next step.

Residential developers · Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Visits are booked over the phone and forgotten, buyers arrive at the wrong gallery or at the busiest hour, and what happened during the visit lives in the executive's head. Interested buyers cool off because nobody follows up with the right unit, floor plan or cost sheet at the right time.

Trigger

A qualified lead accepts a visit in the WhatsApp Flow, an executive books one in the CRM, or a channel partner books one for a registered client.

How it runs

  • Offer visit slots by project and gallery based on executive rosters and weekend capacity, and write the booking to the CRM against the lead and any partner registration.
  • Confirm with an approved template carrying the location pin, parking and what to bring, then send reminders the day before and a few hours before with reschedule and cancel buttons.
  • On arrival, a QR check-in at the gallery records the visit, alerts the assigned executive and confirms attribution for any registered partner.
  • After the visit, the executive dictates or types notes; AI drafts a summary of units shown, objections and next step, which the executive confirms before it is saved.
  • Send a short feedback request and the follow-up content the executive selected, such as the floor plan or cost sheet, and schedule the agreed callback.
  • Show no-shows, revisits and visit-to-booking conversion by project, source, partner and executive.

Human checkpoint

Executives confirm every AI visit summary before it enters the CRM and choose what follow-up content is sent. Cost sheets are generated only from the approved price sheet, and the sales manager reviews hot leads and any negotiation every day.

Visit and evaluateStandard3–5 weeks

NRI buyer nurturing across time zones with video site visits

Buyers abroad get replies and updates in their own daytime, book video site visits that overlap with Indian working hours, and receive answers on eligibility, payments and documentation only from content your legal team approves, with an NRI desk manager owning every relationship.

Residential developers · Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

NRI enquiries arrive overnight Indian time and wait until morning, and follow-ups land in the middle of the buyer's night. Questions about NRE or NRO payments, power of attorney and repatriation get informal, inconsistent answers from different executives, and family members in India are left out of the conversation.

Trigger

A lead is identified as living abroad by its country code, a form answer or the executive's tag in the CRM.

How it runs

  • Record the buyer's country, time zone and preferred contact hours, and collect a WhatsApp and email opt-in that names the developer.
  • Schedule replies, reminders and updates inside the buyer's local daytime, with a live handover to the NRI desk during overlapping hours.
  • Offer a video site visit with an executive at the project, and invite a family member the buyer nominates in India to a physical visit if the buyer wishes.
  • Answer questions on eligibility, payment through NRE, NRO or FCNR accounts or inward remittance, power of attorney and documents only from the FAQ legal approves; tax and individual cases go to the legal team or the buyer's adviser.
  • Send a monthly email digest of construction progress and new releases to opted-in buyers, with an unsubscribe link in every email.
  • Track responses, video visits and bookings by country and source.

Human checkpoint

The NRI desk relationship manager owns each buyer and handles every pricing, booking and documentation conversation. Legal approves the FAQ and the power of attorney guidance, and no automated message gives tax or foreign exchange advice on an individual case.

Visit and evaluateStandard4–6 weeks

Office and co-working enquiries from tour to signed agreement

Enquiries for desks, cabins or office floors are qualified, matched to live inventory, booked into a center tour and followed by a proposal from the approved price book. New members and tenants are onboarded with company KYC, access and billing set up from one record.

Commercial leasing & co-working

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Requirements arrive from consultants, aggregators, Google and walk-ins, and availability lives in a spreadsheet that is rarely current. Tours are arranged over calls across centers, proposals wait for pricing approval by email, and new members wait days for access cards and invoices.

Trigger

An enquiry arrives from the website, Google Business Profile, an aggregator or broker, a WhatsApp message, or a walk-in logged by the community manager.

How it runs

  • Capture seats or area, move-in date, term, budget and location, and attribute the enquiry to the consultant, broker or aggregator where one is involved.
  • Match the requirement to live inventory from the co-working platform or the landlord's stacking plan, and shortlist suitable options.
  • Book a tour with the center or leasing manager, send confirmations and reminders, and offer a day pass where the operator allows it.
  • Generate a proposal from the approved price book within the discount band, with exceptions routed to the center head or leasing director.
  • On acceptance, collect company KYC such as GSTIN and authorized signatory, send the membership agreement or letter of intent for e-signature, and set up access, Wi-Fi and billing.
  • Report enquiry-to-tour time, tour-to-signing conversion, occupancy and lost-deal reasons by center and channel.

Human checkpoint

Community and leasing managers run every tour and negotiation. Discounts outside the approved band need the center head, and lease terms, letters of intent and enterprise agreements are approved by the leasing director and legal before signature.

Book, document and financeAdvanced6–8 weeks

Booking to registered agreement: KYC, allotment and home loans

After a booking, buyers complete a secure application with KYC, the CRM team verifies it, allotment letters and agreement drafts come from legal-approved templates, demands stay within the RERA advance limit until registration, and each home-loan case is tracked with the buyer's lender.

Residential developers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Booking forms, KYC copies, payment proofs, allotment letters and agreement drafts move between sales, CRM, legal, finance and lenders by email and paper. Missing documents delay registration, demands can exceed the advance RERA allows before a registered agreement, and buyers cannot tell where their loan or paperwork stands.

Trigger

A sales executive marks a unit as booked in the CRM or ERP and the booking amount is received through the bank or payment gateway.

How it runs

  • Send the buyer a secure, expiring link to complete the application for every applicant, upload PAN and address proof, or passport and visa details for NRIs, and confirm the unit, price and payment plan.
  • Match the booking amount against bank or gateway records, and block any further demand above the advance RERA permits until the agreement for sale is registered.
  • Queue the file for CRM verification; once verified, generate the allotment letter from the legal-approved template and send it for authorized signature.
  • If the buyer needs a loan, record their consent to share status with the lender they choose, send that lender's checklist and the list of banks that have approved the project, and track sanction and any tripartite agreement.
  • Prepare the agreement for sale from the state's prescribed format for legal review, book the registration appointment, and track stamp duty and registration fees.
  • Keep the buyer informed at each step with approved WhatsApp and email updates, and show every file's status and blocker on a CRM team board.

Human checkpoint

The CRM team verifies every KYC file and legal approves every allotment letter and agreement. Any deviation in price, payment plan or terms needs the sales head and finance controller. Lenders decide loans, and nothing is shared with a lender without the buyer's consent.

Book, document and financeStandard4–5 weeks

Client KYC and PMLA record-keeping for brokerages

As a deal moves toward closure, the brokerage collects client KYC through a secure link, records beneficial ownership and payment details, screens names against the lists its AML policy requires and keeps a five-year record. Possible red flags go privately to the Principal Officer.

Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Brokerages above the PMLA turnover threshold are reporting entities, yet client documents often sit in agents' phones and email. Without a consistent file, the firm cannot show due diligence, retrieve records for the required period or route a concern to the Principal Officer without alerting the client.

Trigger

An agent marks a deal as agreed in principle, or a client is about to pay a token or booking amount on a sale or purchase the brokerage facilitates.

How it runs

  • Send the client, and the other party where the brokerage acts for both, a secure link to upload identity and address documents and, for companies or trusts, beneficial ownership details.
  • Verify documents through an approved verification service where the client consents, and record the method and result.
  • Screen names against the sanctions and other lists the brokerage's AML policy requires, including the UN sanctions list, and hold the file on a possible match.
  • Record payment mode, paying party and a source-of-funds declaration, and flag the patterns the policy defines, such as large cash components, third-party payers or unexplained structures.
  • Send flags only to the Principal Officer's private queue with the evidence; the agent sees that the file is on hold, not why.
  • Keep KYC and transaction records for five years under the record-keeping rules, with an access log and a search for inspections.

Human checkpoint

The Principal Officer reviews every flag and decides whether a report is required; the automation never files with FIU-IND and never contacts the client about a flag. The Designated Director approves the AML policy and screening lists, and the brokerage's legal advisers confirm thresholds and duties.

Book, document and financeStandard4–6 weeks

Brokerage eligibility, invoicing and payout tracking

Every deal's brokerage terms, milestones, invoices and payments sit on one record. Developers and landlords see which partner claims are due and approve them; brokerages see what each developer owes them and how commissions split among their agents.

Brokers & channel partners · Commercial leasing & co-working

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Brokerage depends on booking milestones, agreement registration, payment receipts and slab terms that differ by project and period. Partners send invoices that do not match, finance cannot see what is due, and payouts stall while partners chase sales teams on WhatsApp.

Trigger

A booking or lease reaches the brokerage milestone in the partner agreement, such as agreement registration and receipt of the agreed payment, or the start of a lease.

How it runs

  • Read the deal, milestone status and receipts from the CRM, ERP or lease system, and calculate eligible brokerage from the partner agreement and the project's slab rules.
  • Publish a brokerage statement to the partner portal and invite an invoice, with GSTIN and bank details checked against the empanelment record.
  • Compare the invoice with the statement, send mismatches back to the partner, and route matched invoices for sales or leasing head and finance approval.
  • Post approved payouts to the accounting system, with tax deductions applied by finance, and notify the partner when payment is released.
  • Flag cancellations and refunds that trigger a clawback or adjustment under the agreement, for finance to decide.
  • For brokerages, track receivables by developer and agent splits, and remind owners of invoices unpaid beyond the agreed period.

Human checkpoint

The finance controller approves every payout and every clawback, and the sales or leasing head approves any slab exception. The automation calculates, checks and reminds; it never releases money.

Build and payAdvanced5–7 weeks

Construction progress updates and milestone-linked demand letters

When the project's architect or engineer certifies a construction stage, buyers receive a progress update with photos and a demand letter calculated from their payment plan, once finance approves the batch. Lenders get disbursement requests for loan buyers, and monthly updates fill the gaps.

Residential developers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Demand letters are compiled from the ERP in spreadsheets, checked by hand and sent without evidence that the stage is complete. Buyers and lenders push back, disbursements arrive late and collections slip. Progress updates are irregular and sometimes disagree with what the developer files on the RERA portal.

Trigger

A construction stage in the payment plan, such as a slab or masonry milestone, is certified by the project's architect or engineer and approved by the project head in the ERP, or the monthly update date arrives.

How it runs

  • Collect the stage certificate, site photos and tower-wise progress from the site team's reports, and draft a plain-language update from those facts only.
  • Route the update to the project head and marketing for approval, checking stated progress against the figures in the latest RERA quarterly update.
  • Generate demand letters per unit from the payment plan with amount, taxes, due date and the project's designated collection account, and run a maker-checker review of totals and a sample of letters.
  • Release the approved batch by email with the letter and update, plus a WhatsApp notification with a secure link, and send lenders the disbursement request pack for loan buyers.
  • Remind buyers before the due date, match receipts from bank statements, and pass overdue cases to the CRM team with history; any interest under the agreement is calculated for finance to review, never applied automatically.
  • Show demanded, collected and overdue amounts by tower and milestone, and disbursement requests pending with each lender.

Human checkpoint

No demand goes out without the architect's or engineer's certificate, the project head's approval and the finance controller's batch approval. Interest, waivers and payment-plan changes are decided by finance and the CRM head, and the project head approves every progress statement.

Build and payAdvanced5–8 weeks

Daily site reports, labor attendance and material approvals

Site engineers file one mobile daily report covering work done against plan, photos, manpower by subcontractor, equipment, materials received and material requests. Attendance is reconciled, requests are checked against BOQ balance and routed by value, and managers get a daily digest.

Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Progress, labor counts and material needs arrive as WhatsApp photos, calls and paper registers. Project managers see slippage days late, subcontractor bills cannot be checked against actual manpower, and materials are ordered without checking BOQ balance or site stock.

Trigger

The site engineer opens the daily report before the end of the shift, or raises a material request between reports.

How it runs

  • Collect activities and quantities against the planned schedule, location-tagged photos, manpower by trade and subcontractor, equipment hours, materials received with challan photos, and hindrances, in a mobile form that also works offline.
  • Pull headcount from biometric or app-based attendance and flag gaps against the manpower reported for each subcontractor.
  • Check each material request against the BOQ balance, the current drawing revision and site stock, and flag requests above balance for the quantity surveyor.
  • Route requests for approval by value, from site in-charge to project manager to purchase head, with purchase raising the order in the ERP.
  • Compare reported progress with the schedule baseline, and send the project manager a daily digest of slippage, idle labor, stock risks and open issues.
  • Compile a weekly progress report with photos for the client or developer, reviewed by the project manager before it is shared.

Human checkpoint

The project manager reviews the daily digest and approves material requests within their limit; the purchase head approves higher values and the quantity surveyor approves anything above BOQ balance. Subcontractor bills are certified by the project manager and accounts, not by the automation.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Schedule in Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project
  • Site apps such as Powerplay or Procore
  • Biometric or app-based attendance
  • ERP such as SAP or Tally for purchase orders and stock
  • BOQ and drawing registers

Data & consent

Worker data is limited to name, ID, trade, subcontractor and attendance times; biometric templates stay in the attendance device or vendor system and are never copied. Photos show work, not faces, wherever possible. Attendance and wage-related records are kept for the periods labor rules require, with access limited to site administration and HR.

What we deliver

  • Offline-capable daily report form
  • Attendance reconciliation by subcontractor

  • Daily digest and weekly client report
  • Site dashboard by project

How we measure it

  • Manpower variance between attendance and reports
  • Material request approval time
  • Requests above BOQ balance
  • Schedule variance by activity

Build and payStandard3–5 weeks

Safety incident and near-miss logging with immediate escalation

Anyone on site can report an injury, dangerous occurrence or near miss by WhatsApp or QR code, with photos. Serious events trigger immediate calls to the safety officer and project head, corrective actions are tracked, and statutory notices are drafted for the responsible person to file.

Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Near misses go unreported, serious incidents are relayed by phone with details lost, and the statutory notices and registers that labor law requires depend on one person remembering the deadlines. Corrective actions from one site rarely reach the next.

Trigger

A worker, supervisor or engineer scans the site safety QR code or messages the site safety number, or a toolbox talk or inspection records an unsafe condition.

How it runs

  • Capture what happened, where, who was involved, any injuries, photos and immediate actions in a short form offered in the languages used on site.
  • Classify severity using the safety officer's rules; fatal accidents, serious injuries and dangerous occurrences such as a scaffold or structure collapse trigger immediate calls and messages to the safety officer, site in-charge and project head.
  • Open an investigation record with timeline, witnesses, root-cause fields and corrective actions with owners and due dates.
  • Draft statutory notices and register entries from the record for the safety officer to complete and file within the deadlines the applicable rules set.
  • Track corrective actions to closure with photo evidence, and share lessons across sites in a weekly safety bulletin.
  • Report incidents, near misses, open actions and toolbox talk coverage by site and subcontractor.

Human checkpoint

The site safety officer owns every report and decides severity, investigation and closure; first aid, medical care and emergency response never wait for the automation. The safety officer or employer files statutory notices, and the system only drafts and reminds. The project head reviews serious incidents that day.

Records are kept for the period the applicable labor rules and the contractor's insurer require, and reporters can stay anonymous for near misses.

Possession and move-inStandard4–6 weeks

Possession, fit-out handover and snag-list management

After the occupancy certificate or fit-out completion, buyers and tenants book handover slots, receive a final dues statement, report snags room by room with photos and track each item as the contractor fixes it and a quality engineer verifies it. Later defect reports follow the same path.

Residential developers · Commercial leasing & co-working · Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Possession arrives in a rush: buyers call for dates and final dues, snag lists are written on paper during the walkthrough, and contractors receive them days later on WhatsApp. Items are closed without proof and reopened by unhappy buyers, and defect complaints after handover get lost although the developer remains responsible for years.

Trigger

The occupancy certificate is received and possession is offered for a tower, or a commercial floor's warm-shell or fit-out handover is ready; later, an owner or tenant reports a defect.

How it runs

  • Send the possession or handover offer with the final dues statement and document checklist, and offer handover slots by tower and floor.
  • During the pre-handover inspection, buyers or tenants log snags room by room with photos and a category, on a tablet with the handover executive or on their own phone.
  • Assign each snag to the responsible contractor or trade with a due date, and notify the contractor's site engineer.
  • Contractors close items with after photos, and the quality engineer verifies each closure before the buyer or tenant is asked to confirm.
  • Release keys or access once dues, documents and the agreed snags are complete, and record the handover acknowledgement.
  • Keep a defect reporting route open after handover, tracked as defect-liability tickets with the same assignment and verification steps.

Human checkpoint

The quality engineer verifies every closure and the CRM handover manager signs off each possession. Disputed snags, compensation questions and any structural concern go to the project head and, where needed, the structural consultant.

  • Real estate CRM or lease system

  • Facility helpdesk for post-handover defects

Data & consent

Uses unit, owner or tenant contact, dues status and snag photos of the property only. Contractors see the unit, location and snag, never buyer contact details. Handover and defect records are kept for at least the defect liability period, which RERA sets at five years from possession for units sold in registered projects.

What we deliver

  • Possession offer, dues and slot booking flow
  • Snag capture app with photo evidence
  • Contractor assignment and verification workflow
  • Defect-liability ticketing
  • Handover and snag dashboard

How we measure it

  • Offer-to-handover time
  • Snags closed by due date
  • Snag reopen rate
  • Defect tickets open beyond target
  • Handover satisfaction score

Occupy, renew and referStandard4–6 weeks

Lease abstraction, rent, escalation and renewal reminders

Key dates and terms are extracted from signed leases and verified by the leasing manager. Rent invoices and reminders follow the lease calendar, escalations are calculated for finance to approve, and renewal and lock-in dates reach the asset manager early enough to act.

Commercial leasing & co-working

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Escalation, lock-in, notice and renewal terms are buried in signed PDFs and a spreadsheet nobody fully trusts. Escalations are billed late or wrongly, receivables age without follow-up, and renewal talks start only when a tenant serves notice.

Trigger

A new lease or membership agreement is signed, or a calendar event arrives: rent due, escalation date, lock-in expiry, renewal notice window or security deposit review.

How it runs

  • Extract parties, area, rent, escalation clause, lock-in, notice period, renewal options, deposit and fit-out terms from the signed lease into a structured abstract with page references.
  • Hold each abstract until the leasing manager verifies every field against the lease, then load the dates into the lease calendar.
  • Trigger rent invoices with GST through accounts, send reminders before and after the due date, and pass overdue cases to the asset manager with history.
  • Calculate escalations from the clause and send the draft letter for finance approval before it reaches the tenant.
  • Alert the asset manager ahead of lock-in expiry and renewal notice windows with occupancy, payment history and open helpdesk tickets for that tenant.
  • Track renewal proposals and exits, including deposit reconciliation and the handback inspection.

Human checkpoint

The leasing manager verifies every abstract before any date is used. Finance approves escalation letters and invoices, legal approves notices, and the asset manager decides renewal terms and any rent concession.

Tools

ACAnthropic ClaudeSSupabasenn8nRRetoolRResendMPMicrosoft Power BI

  • Co-working platform such as Nexudus or OfficeRnD
  • Accounting such as Tally or SAP
  • Signed lease document storage

Data & consent

Uses lease terms, tenant company contacts and payment history. Leases stay in the landlord's document store, and extraction runs under terms that exclude training on the data. Access is limited to leasing, finance and legal, and abstracts and correspondence are kept for the lease term plus the period tax and contract records require.

What we deliver

  • Verified lease abstracts with page references
  • Lease calendar with owner alerts
  • Rent and escalation workflow with finance approval
  • Renewal pipeline and receivables dashboard

How we measure it

  • Rent collected by due date
  • Escalations billed on time
  • Renewals decided before notice deadline
  • Abstract fields corrected at verification
  • Receivables by age
